newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani police arrest Bhutto servant.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani police arrest Bhutto servant.

text.p: Pakistani police have raided the home of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto and arrested one of her servants, a spokesman for Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) said on Wednesday.
The spokesman said the servant, Irshad Ahmed Pholputo, 23, had been arrested on Tuesday at Bhutto's farmhouse in Naudero, near the town of Larkana, in the southern province of Sindh.
He described the police action as "political victimisation" against Bhutto by the caretaker government in Sindh province, which is headed by her estranged cousin Mumtaz Ali Bhutto.
Police, denying any political motive, said they had charged Pholputo with illegally hunting migratory birds.
"There is no truth to the PPP charges which have been blown out of proportion," a police officer said.
Bhutto herself said in a statement from Naudero that the police raid had been illegal and demanded Pholputo's release.

Bhutto, dismissed in November by President Farooq Leghari on disputed charges of corruption and misrule, led the PPP to a crushing defeat in last week's national and provincial elections. The Pakistan Muslim League, headed by Nawaz Sharif, won a massive majority.

In Karachi, police said they wanted to arrest Bhutto's father-in-law, Hakim Ali Zardari, on a charge of fraudulently obtaining a loan in the 1970s, and had raided several places in search of him. A spokesman for Zardari denied the charge.

Bhutto's husband, Asif Ali Zardari, has been detained by police since her government was ousted on November 5, and faces a charge of conspiring to murder her brother Murtaza in September. Zardari denies any part in Murtaza's killing.
